title: Contractive i-ResNet residual task views
hypothesis: A low-rank shared residual basis supports distinct contractive block functions with exact forward quality and convergent fixed-point inverse while reducing complete bytes versus independent residual matrices.

development.selection_metric: heldout output nRMSE, inverse convergence/error, Lipschitz/singular-value margins, actual bytes and MACs

fresh.reason: synthetic rank-2 residual screen; exact native factorization attribution assessed first

success_gate: Heldout output nRMSE <=0.02; inverse converged on all samples with error <=1e-5; teacher Lipschitz <1; >=25% fewer complete bytes; strict quality/byte/compute gain over native basis and scalar FiLM.
failure_gate: Invertibility/stability, quality, storage or compute gate miss, or exact native basis payload/function alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
amendments: A01 before final scoring: all methods use the same fixed heldout input matrices after initial evaluation accidentally drew a different test set per method. Initial unpaired values are preserved in RESULTS_INITIAL_UNPAIRED_INPUTS.csv; no seed or gate changed.
boundaries: Synthetic linear contractive residual blocks only; matrices are generated from a shared rank-2 basis.
No trained i-ResNet, image model, reversible-memory training or accelerator inverse-runtime claim.
SVD basis and heldout codes are oracle-estimated from operator calibration outputs; this is not end-to-end training.
